Text: The Wardens

Machines stranded in a poisoned wasteland. They run on badwater, their industry kills the soil, and the only thing they value is Data. Their purpose: make the land livable for beavers again, and remember enough to bring back the ones who came before.
The Ark is complete.
Every observation, every failure, every season of green: archived. The Wardens spend it all on a single question. What if the old ones came back?

The Core
District center and reactor. Every Warden reports here, and the Core's 150 hp of power runs the first machines.
It was never meant to run this long. It has not stopped.
Charging Post
A Warden standing here recharges. Needs 50 hp of power.
Power is life.
The Cruncher
Turns power into Science Points, or Badwater and Scrap Metal into Data Cores. Never both.
Research burns power. Choose what to think about.
Sludge Burner
Burns Biomass from Sludge Reed for 200 hp of power. Poisons the ground around it.
The first ecological debt. It will not be the last.
Reed Bed
Plants and harvests Sludge Reed, the only crop that grows in poisoned soil.
Something grows here. Nobody said it had to be pretty.
Sludge Reed
Thrives on contamination. Harvested for Biomass.

Breeding Pod
Grows a new beaver from Biomass. Needs 100 hp of power. The pod the Iron Teeth will inherit.
The first thing the Wardens ever built for someone else.
Advanced Breeding Pod
Grows an adult beaver from Biomass and Firmware. Needs 150 hp of power.
It comes out knowing things. Nobody is sure that is a kindness.
Sludge Pump
Pumps Badwater, the only liquid this land has to offer. Wardens work it without complaint.
Do not drink. Nobody here drinks.
Badwater Cell
Burns Badwater for 100 hp of power. Cheap, dirty, and the first thing that keeps the lights on.
The Wardens run on badwater. So does everything they build.
Planter Rig
Plants trees and bushes in its range. Nothing grows here yet; one day it will.
Directive 2, in hardware.
Crate Rack
Stores one kind of boxed good, Biomass included. Set the good after selecting the rack.
Everything in its place. The Wardens like it that way.
Hauler Dock
Wardens stationed here carry goods around the district wherever they are needed.
Someone has to carry it. Nobody said it had to be the builder.
Observation Deck
A place to stand and look at the land. Beavers gather here, and their well-being rises.
Directive 3: record everything. The view is part of the record.
Cold Boot

SYSTEM RESTART.

The uptime counter overflowed 3,000 days ago. Sensors report no growth, no water worth drinking, no beavers.

Five Wardens online. Power: the Core, and nothing else.

We were not built to live here. We were built so that others could.

Directive 1: keep the machines running.
Directive 2: make this land livable.
Directive 3: record everything. One day, someone will need to know how.
Basics

First, a survey of the site. Move the view across the ground.

Look for ruins. The old world left its metal behind, and metal is the only thing this ground still gives.
Now rotate the view. Ruins hide behind ruins.
Zoom in to inspect a single Warden, or pull back to see the whole site.

Time runs whether we are ready or not.

Pause when you need to think. The Wardens will wait. They are good at waiting.
Speed up when there is nothing to decide. Wardens do not tire of working, and you should not tire of watching them.
Scrap

There is no wood here. There is scrap.

Only scavengers collect Scrap Metal, and only from ruins within their flag's range. Place two Scavenger Flags beside the ruins.

The Flags will not be built unless they are in the district's building range.

Select the Core to see its range. Paths connected to the Core's entrance extend it.

Every building with an entrance must be connected to the Core with a Path. Select a building to see its entrance marked by an arrow.

Build Paths to connect the Scavenger Flags to the Core.

Scrap Metal is the only material this land gives freely.

Gather ten. Everything the Wardens will ever build starts as someone else's wreckage.
Badwater and Biomass

Wardens do not drink. They do need Badwater: it feeds the generators and, later, the Data Cores.

Build a Sludge Pump on a badwater source and connect it to the Core.

Power is life. A Warden that runs dry stops where it stands, and it does not get up again.

Build a Charging Post next to the Core. Then select a Warden and read its Energy; keep every unit above half charge.

Directive 2 needs something that grows. Sludge Reed grows in poisoned soil, and its Biomass will feed the pods.

Build a Reed Bed. Like flags, it has a limited range.

The Reed Bed does not start working until you tell it what and where to plant.

Use the Plant Crops tool to designate a Sludge Reed field. Reed asks for no irrigation. It asks for nothing at all.
Working hours

Wardens do not sleep, but the Core sets a shift length for everything that works here.

Longer shifts mean faster progress and a faster drain on the units. For now, extend the shift a little.
Storage

Many buildings have some built-in storage, and it fills up quickly.

Build a Scrap Pile. Each storage building holds a single good; set it after selecting the building.

All liquids are stored in tanks, Badwater included.

Build two Sludge Tanks and set them to Badwater.

Biomass is a boxed good, and boxed goods go in racks.

Build a Crate Rack and set it to Biomass before the first harvest comes in.
Science

Metal is not the goal. Knowledge is.

Build the Cruncher and connect it to the Core with a Power Shaft. The Core can barely run it; that is the point.

For now, let the Cruncher think.

Once enough Science Points accumulate, we will spend them to unlock what the Wardens forgot how to build.
Pods

We were built so that others could live here. Breeding Pods grow beavers from Biomass.

Build two Breeding Pods. They stay dark until they have power; that comes next.
Power and pods

The Core cannot feed everything. Wardens run on what this land has: Badwater.

Build a Badwater Cell. It burns Badwater from the Sludge Pump for 100 hp of power.

Connect the Cell to a Breeding Pod with Power Shafts.

Tip: buildings placed wall to wall pass power to each other. No shafts needed.
First beaver

A pod needs power and Biomass, then five days.

Wait for the first beaver. It will not know what the Wardens are. It will not need to.
Reforestation

Directive 2: make this land livable.

Using Science Points from the Cruncher, unlock the Planter Rig. Then build it where you want trees to grow.

Use the Plant Trees and Bushes tool to plant Birches. They grow quickly and ask for little.

Trees only grow on irrigated, green ground. Find some. There is not much.
Maintenance

You can see the state of every unit.

Select a Warden by clicking on it. Its panel shows Energy, attributes and needs. A need at zero has consequences.

The settlement's average well-being is shown in the top left corner.

Click it to see every need and how well it is met. Wardens have few needs. The beavers will have more.

Long shifts drain Wardens faster than the Charging Posts can fill them.

For now, return to the default working hours.
Dams

Tanks hold Badwater for a while. Long-term survival depends on taming the flow of water.

Build a line of Dams across the nearest river, bank to bank, and observe what happens.
Vertical architecture

Space is scarce in the wasteland. The Wardens build upward.

Some buildings have flat roofs that can support other structures. Build an Observation Deck on one; you may need Stairs to connect it.
Droughts

The settlement has survived its first drought.

Droughts are part of the seasonal cycle. They return, and each one lasts longer.

If you have not built a dam, build one before the next.
Badtides

The settlement has weathered its first badtide.

Badwater is nothing new to the Wardens, but the beavers and the reeds are not so indifferent. Future badtides will not be as forgiving.
Haulers and workforce

As the settlement grows, it moves more goods. Transport takes a large part of a unit's shift.

Haulers help. They move goods around the entire district, following demand. Build a Hauler Dock.

Some workplaces, the Hauler Dock included, do not fill all their slots by default. Change the desired number of workers in the building's panel.

Workplace priorities control staffing too. The Dock can usually run on low priority. Try both now.

Buildings and construction sites can be paused. Paused workplaces are vacated at once and the units reassign themselves.

Select the Hauler Dock and pause it from its panel.
Layer tool

As the settlement grows upward, working beneath buildings gets difficult.

The Layer tool hides everything above the selected layer. Change the visible layer with the highlighted buttons.
The visible layer also has key bindings, like most actions. Find them in tooltips or in the Settings menu.

Scrap in hand. The Sludge Pump, Reed Bed, Sludge Tank and Crate Rack are now available.
Chapter 3: Signal.
Shifts are set. The Cruncher is now available: power in, Science or Data Cores out.
Chapter 4: Pods.
Stores are full. The Breeding Pod is now available. Built for someone else.
Chapter 5: Power.
The pods are waiting. The Badwater Cell and the Sludge Burner are now available. Every hour of power is an hour of poison.
Chapter 6: Green.
The first beaver is awake. The Advanced Breeding Pod is now available.
Nothing has grown here in 3,000 days.
We were not built to live here. We were built so that others could.
